subject: FinTrust: request for exception to multi-region RTO/RPO commitments
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@fintrust.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: Priyanka Rao <priyanka@fintrust.com>, legal@fintrust.com
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: multi-region DR / RTO/RPO exception for regulated workloads

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. As we dug into our compliance matrix, we realized a challenge: our primary regulator requires that certain customer-facing transaction logs be retained and reconciled from a single region for up to 90 minutes before cross-region replication is allowed. Practically that means we cannot failover to a secondary region and assert full transactional consistency until up to 1 hour of data can be reconciled (RPO ~1hr). Additionally, our internal ops policy requires a controlled failover window for key payment flows that can extend RTO to up to 3 hours while the reconciliation and audit run.

Can Redwood agree to an SLA carveout for these specific FinTrust workloads (account IDs prefixed FT-PRD-*) that permits an RPO up to 1 hour and RTO up to 3 hours for cross-region failover, with the following controls in place:
- Monthly joint DR exercise with Redwood ops (reporting results)
- Retention of audit logs for 13 months and delivery of logs on request within 48 hours
- Enhanced tracing for any failover event (request id correlation)

We understand this is an exception to Redwood's standard multi-region guarantees; we are prepared to accept a commercial concession or SLA credit in exchange. I’ve attached a short requirements doc. Can you route this to the right people?

Sanjay Mehta
Head of Infrastructure Operations
FinTrust Bank

Attachments: FinTrust_DR_requirements_2028.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@fintrust.com>
Cc: Priyanka Rao <priyanka@fintrust.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region DR / RTO/RPO exception for regulated workloads

Sanjay — thanks for sending this over and for the clear ask. Looping in Neha (solutions) and Marcus (product) for technical assessment and Laura (legal) for contract impacts.

Quick notes from my side:
- We can absolutely operate on customer-scoped carveouts (we do this in Dedicated/Private for a handful of regulated customers).
- Tradeoffs to call out: a longer RTO window usually limits some of our automated cross-region read routing and may require a controlled manual failover playbook; there is an operational cost and some availability exposure.
- Commercially, customers who request higher operational overhead typically accept an SLA credit or a dedicated runbook fee.

Neha/Marcus — can you review FinTrust_DR_requirements_2028.pdf and reply with (a) whether the RTO/RPO numbers are feasible from an operational standpoint and (b) what monitoring/audit hooks we need to enable to meet their log/tracing requirements?

Laura — if this is feasible technically, can we get a redlined amendment that covers: scope (FT-PRD-*), explicit deviation to standard RTO/RPO for those resources, required monthly DR exercises, log delivery SLA, and the commercial credit?

I’ll hold on sending any proposal to FinTrust until we have a quick internal alignment.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-amendment-v1.docx (draft)

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Apr 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: multi-region DR / RTO/RPO exception for regulated workloads

Aditya / Marcus — digging in on the ops side. Summary of feasibility and recommended controls below: 

Feasibility:
- RPO of up to 1 hour: technically feasible if we disable asynchronous immediate cross-region replication for the FT-PRD-* shard set and rely on our batch replication window (we'll keep a write-ahead log retained in the primary region).
- RTO up to 3 hours: feasible as a controlled/manual failover. Automated failover (under 30 mins) is incompatible with the regulator reconciliation step.

Operational controls to require (minimum):
- Monthly joint DR exercise with a documented playbook and post-mortem (we can provide the playbook template).
- Enable persistent audit/tracing collection (retain for 13 months) and a pre-authorized log export process (S3 presigned or secure transfer).
- On failover event, Redwood will provide a failover timeline and request/tx id list within 4 hours and full log export within 48 hours.
- Add a Canary/traffic gating period for 24 hours post-failover to allow FinTrust to validate reconciliation.

Costs/impact:
- Enabling these controls requires a small ops-on-call addendum and additional storage for extended log retention. Estimated recurring fee: $6,000/month; one-time runbook onboarding: $8,500. Alternatively, we can structure this as an SLA credit (we estimate 10–15% on the affected SLAs).

Next steps (internal): Marcus, can you confirm whether product can emit the trace correlation headers required or if we need a short engineering spike? If so, estimate the effort.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sanjay / Aditya — thanks for the details. We reviewed the technical proposal and consulted with product and finance. Redwood is prepared to grant a conditional exception for the FinTrust FT-PRD-* workloads under the following terms (summary):

1) Scope: Applies only to resources that are explicitly listed in Exhibit A (to be attached). Deviations do not apply to other account resources.
2) RTO/RPO carveout: RPO up to 1 hour; RTO up to 3 hours for cross-region failover events initiated for regulatory reconciliation purposes or explicit joint failover exercises.
3) Controls & obligations:
   - Monthly joint DR exercises with documented playbooks and a post-exercise report; Redwood to attend and provide runbook updates as needed.
   - Redwood to retain audit/tracing logs for 13 months and provide export within 48 hours of a request.
   - 24-hour canary gating post-failover during which certain automated traffic-shifting features will be suspended.
4) Commercials: A 12% SLA service credit on impacted SLAs applied monthly for the scoped resources OR optional $6,000/month managed runbook fee + one-time onboarding fee of $8,500. Redwood reserves the right to choose the fee structure if the customer does not select within 14 days.
5) Reporting & acceptance: FinTrust must execute monthly exercises for a minimum of 6 months; continued exception is contingent on satisfactory exercise results.
6) Legal: Amendment to the MSA with Exhibit A listing FT resources and the specific carveout language; standard indemnities and limitations remain unchanged.

I’ve uploaded a draft amendment and a DocuSign link for execution. Please review and let me know if we can proceed to signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
